expectations.text: Recommends extracting the shared Avatar component (NOT keeping 12 inline copies)
expectations.evidence: 'Extract the shared <Avatar/>' and bottom line 'the textbook case for extraction... Extract it.'

expectations.text: Grounds it in the pure-presentation / understood-in-isolation test (low external context to consume)
expectations.evidence: 'It's a purely presentational unit... The test that matters... is can this concern be understood in isolation? Avatar passes that test trivially... edit it confidently with zero external context.'

expectations.text: Rejects the 'keep inline for self-containment' argument as misapplied to a reusable primitive
expectations.evidence: 'that argument only wins when the cross-file lookup actually costs the agent something... Avatar is the exact opposite.' The principle is 'worth keeping for the cases it fits: smart, stateful components... Avatar isn't one of those.'

expectations.text: Frames the shared component as a real abstraction (read at call site without opening internals), not just DRY
expectations.evidence: 'The import is a real abstraction with an interface, not a relocated blob — it hides the implementation, so the consuming code is understandable without reading the internals.'
